newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Hoechst shares tumble after results.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hoechst shares tumble after results.

text.p: Shares in German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG plummeted on Tuesday after the group announced its 1996 results which included a lower than hoped- for dividend payout.

Hoechst shares, the biggest losers in afternoon trading, dropped as low as five percent to 75.02 marks ($43.98) after the group said it would raise its dividend payment to 1.40 marks from 1.30 marks, recovering to 76.76 marks, down 3.03 percent.
Late last week talk swirled around the market that Hoechst, standing to make large extraordinary gains through divestments, might double its dividend payout to 2.60 marks.
Group pre-tax profit, buoyed largely by earnings from spinoffs which brought in about 2.5 billion marks before taxes, soared 29 percent to 5.28 billion marks, Hoechst said in a mandatory statement.
Sales however slipped two percent to 50.9 billion marks, again due largely to divestments, the company said.
Analysts had predicted that sales would fall an average three percent percent but pre-tax profit was expected to surge 50 percent.
Hoechst said business had developed positively in general, but that the chemicals markets in Europe lacked needed buoyancy.

Separately Hoechst said its supervisory board had approved plans to transform the group into a strategic managment holding company, plans Hoechst had announced last fall in a bid to raise value for shareholders.

As part of an aggressive streamlining, Hoechst also announced it planned to spin off its diagnostics business but that it Hoechst would initially continue running the business in the form of a joint-venture. Hoechst declined to name the partner.
